statement: If both singleton additions must strictly decrease Kemeny's constant while the joint addition strictly increases it, the minimum order in the same graph class is seven.
derivation: Every strict-singleton witness is a witness for the frozen nonincreasing-singleton predicate.
The complete original census has no weak-predicate witnesses on fewer than six vertices, and exactly one recorded weak-predicate pair at six vertices.
That six-vertex pair has an exactly zero second-singleton delta, so it does not satisfy the strict-singleton predicate.
The already fixed, published and exactly replayed P7 has singleton deltas -1/14 and -1/14 and joint delta +1/24, so it supplies a strict-singleton witness on seven vertices.
The lower exclusion through six and the fixed order-seven witness together imply minimum seven; no order-seven census or new numerical search is involved.
limits: This corollary was identified after the primary results were known and is not described as the preregistered primary question.
The published P7 example and its phenomenon remain credited to prior work.
Neither this deduction nor a search miss establishes publication novelty.
The historical author explanation's no-alternative-theorem statement described that earlier artifact's scope; it is not rewritten.
